extracted.intended_audience: investigators applying for NIH extramural funding, current NIH grantees, institutional research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: News and policy updates relevant to preparing and managing NIH extramural grant applications and awards, including guidance on model selection, application formats, data management and sharing plans, replication/reproducibility expectations, and recent peer-review and program changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select the most appropriate experimental models (including NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize model choice based on the specific research question; New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) are encouraged where scientifically appropriate, but model selection must be justified by fit to the question and translational relevance. Provide rationale in applications for why chosen models are the best for the stated aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects application format and award structure
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s Collaborative International Research Projects (PF5) has a specific award structure and application format; applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review the PF5 overview (NIH video ~6 minutes) to learn key features and application formatting requirements, and be aware that an application could be administratively split into linked awards post-review and prior to JIT. Prepare proposals with potential linked-award scenarios in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format has been issued, based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for applicable submissions, follow the 2026 pilot format and include the specified (simplified) required elements. Consult the new resource to ensure compliance with NIH expectations for data management and sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility throughout applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability of biomedical research is foundational; NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. NIH launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications and award activities should include considerations, plans, or activities that promote replication and reproducibility where relevant. Expect NIH to highlight and incentivize replication efforts (e.g., highlighted topics) and to consider such plans in evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret the 'Competitive but Not Discussed' review designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications to review processes after resumption of activities, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who receive a 'competitive but not discussed' score should understand this reflects placement in the middle third under the modified process and indicates the application was considered competitive but not selected for discussion. Familiarize yourself with NIH's explanation of the designation and its implications for resubmission and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate effects of centralized peer review under CSR
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH centralized peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR); consolidation aims to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware of changes in peer-review administration and potential impacts on review timelines, study section composition, and competition. Monitor NIH updates explaining how centralization may affect application handling and review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor reinstated NIH Small Business (Seed Fund) program opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s Small Business Program (Seed Fund) has been reinstated and is available to innovators, founders, and R&D-driven small companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses and startups should note the program’s return and review relevant solicitations, eligibility, and application timelines to take advantage of Seed Fund opportunities.
